passive of взволнова́ть (vzvolnovátʹ)
начать волноваться, колыхаться, прийти в колебательное состояние

examples.text: Царь морской является воочию и покровительствует тем, кто его чествует. Когда он распляшется, взволнуются море и реки.

glosses: прийти в возбуждённое состояние, начать волноваться, тревожиться
перен., устар. начать проявлять недовольство существующим положением или действиями властей, поднять мятеж

examples.text: А в Стразбурге начинается новый бунт. Весь здешний гарнизон взволновался.

translations.source_sense_description: начать волноваться, колыхаться, прийти в колебательное состояние

glosses: A sudden transient rush, flood or increase.

examples.text: As President Obama turns his attention once again to filling out a cabinet and writing an Inaugural Address, this much is clear: he should not expect to bask in a surge of national unity, or to witness a crowd of millions overrun the Mall just to say they were there.
He felt a surge of excitement.

glosses: The maximum amplitude of a vehicle's forward/backward oscillation.
A sudden electrical spike or increase of voltage and current.

examples.text: A power surge at that generator created a blackout across the whole district.
When the diesel was being worked full out, the ammeter normally showed about 1,500-1,600 amps, with occasional surges of current at starting or up the steepest gradients to 1,700 or even 1,800 amps.

glosses: A momentary reversal of the airflow through the compressor section of a jet engine due to disruption of the airflow entering the engine's air intake, accompanied by loud banging noises, emission of flame, and temporary loss of thrust.
The swell or heave of the sea (FM 55-501).

examples.text: He that doubteth is like the surge of the sea driven by the wind and tossed.
He flies aloft, and, with impetuous roar, / Pursues the foaming surges to the shore.

glosses: A deployment in large numbers at short notice.

examples.text: surge capacity; surge fleet; surge deployment capabilities

glosses: A spring; a fountain.

examples.text:
1523-1525, John Bourchier, 2nd Baron Berners, Froissart's Chronicles
all great rivers are gorged and assembled of various surges and springs of water

glosses: The tapered part of a windlass barrel or a capstan, upon which the cable surges, or slips.
To rush, flood, or increase suddenly.

examples.text: Toaster sales surged last year.

Carried somehow, somewhither, for some reason, on these surging floods, were these travelers, of errand not wholly obvious to their fellows, yet of such sort as to call into query alike the nature of their errand and their own relations.

Athletes' use of herbal supplements has skyrocketed in the past two decades. At the top of the list of popular herbs are echinacea and ginseng, whereas garlic, St. John's wort, soybean, ephedra and others are also surging in popularity or have been historically prevalent.

glosses: To accelerate forwards, particularly suddenly.

examples.text: A ship surges forwards, sways sideways and heaves up.

Wales began the second half as they ended the first, closing down Montenegro quickly and the pressure told as Bale surged into the box and pulled the ball back for skipper Ramsey, arriving on cue, to double their lead.

glosses: To experience a momentary reversal of airflow through the compressor section due to disruption of intake airflow.

examples.text: Use of maximum reverse thrust at low speeds can cause the engine to surge from ingesting its own exhaust.

glosses: To slack off a line.

translations.source_sense_description: начать волноваться, колыхаться, прийти в колебательное состояние

glosses: A moving disturbance, or undulation, in the surface of a fluid.

examples.text: I dropped a small stone into the pond and watched the ripples spread.
The ebbing tide had left ripples in the sand.
Ripples in the water betray the presence of the fish waiting for a chance to pounce on the insects skirting over the water.

glosses: A sound similar to that of undulating water.
A style of ice cream in which flavors have been coarsely blended together.

examples.text: I enjoy fudge ripple ice cream, but I especially like to dig through the carton to get at the ripple part and eat only that.

glosses: A small oscillation of an otherwise steady signal.
To move like the undulating surface of a body of water; to undulate.

examples.text: Investments in research, deployment and scaling existing technologies are the initial ripples that will have to build to a groundswell of further action.

glosses: To propagate like a moving wave.

examples.text: These problems were complicated by a foreign exchange crunch which rippled through the economy in 1961-1962, […]

glosses: To make a sound as of water running gently over a rough bottom, or the breaking of ripples on the shore.
To shape into a series of ripples.
To launch or unleash in rapid succession.

examples.text: Hearns' 'Mech rippled fifteen missiles. Austen watched the missiles go in. They smashed into a copse of trees, smashing the trunks aside.

glosses: To scratch, tear, or break slightly; graze

examples.text: An horsemans javelin[…]having slightly rippled the skinne of his left arme, pierced within his short ribs.

glosses: An implement, with teeth like those of a comb, for removing the seeds and seed vessels from flax, broom corn, etc.
To remove the seeds from (the stalks of flax, etc.), by means of a ripple.

glosses: Dar forma de olas u ondas.

examples.text: María, sacudiendo estremecida la cabeza, hizo ondular los bucles de su cabellera, y escondiendo en mi pecho la faz, extendió uno de los brazos para señalarme el altar.

glosses: Moverse o agitarse asemejando las olas.

examples.text: Una niña estaba en la terraza de la fonda, rubia como las muñecas, cuya melena rizada le caía sobre el guardapolvo de dril ondulando en el gentil balanceo de los brazos y sujeta por una diadema de piedras verdes.

glosses: Propio o natural de una onda.

examples.text: La ceremonia inaugural fue de escaso valor espectacular. Tan sólo el público, que se movía acompasadamente y realizaba movimientos ondulares, animó el acto».

translations.source_sense_description: начать волноваться, колыхаться, прийти в колебательное состояние

glosses: Mover o agitar produciendo ondas.

examples.text: Recuerdo que cuando el buque // de la orilla se alejaba, // a mi madre oí que enviaba // su despedida postrer: // corrí a la popa, y entonces // la vi ondear su pañuelo, // y luego mirar el cielo, // y desmayarse, y caer.

glosses: Formarse ondas en un fluido.

examples.text: En atléticos juegos gasta sin tasa, // y en circos e hipodromos el día pasa; // sobre el Bósforo manso, que ante ella ondea, // en góndolas de noche canta y pasea;

glosses: Moverse o agitarse asemejando las olas.

examples.text: ¡Oh! Cuántas veces su cabello rubio, // al blando aliento de la fresca brisa, // velón ondeaba, y en feliz desorden // ¡Vino a mi frente!
